item.text: The session is a database-backed opaque token, and the workspace role is looked up separately from that session. I’m checking the exact expiry, navigation, and permission paths so the explanation reflects what the code actually does.

The sign-in form starts with validation on both sides of the request. In [login-form.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/app/(auth)/login/login-form.tsx), `LoginForm` uses `useActionState` to parse the submitted email, password and `rememberMe` with `loginSchema` from [auth.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/schemas/auth.ts). The schema validates and lowercases the email and requires a nonempty password. Client validation supplies field errors; `loginAction` validates again on the server.

[login.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/actions/auth/login.ts) calls `consumeRateLimit` for the anonymous `auth:login` bucket, then calls `login` in [auth-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/server/services/auth-service.ts). The service also consumes that same anonymous bucket before checking credentials, so a request that reaches it is charged twice. It uses `findUserByEmail` and `findPasswordHash` in [user-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts). An unknown user and an incorrect password produce the same credentials-mismatch message. `verifyPassword` in [hash.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/lib/hash.ts) derives a key with scrypt using the stored salt and compares it with the stored key using `timingSafeEqual`; the password hash is kept out of the ordinary `User` type.

On success, `login` calls `createSessionToken` in [session-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/server/services/session-service.ts). It generates 32 random bytes encoded as a URL-safe token, sets an expiry 30 days ahead, and passes the token’s SHA-256 hash to `createSession` in [session-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/server/repositories/session-repository.ts). The database row stores its own ID, the user ID, a null initial `activeOrgId`, the **hash**, expiry and timestamps. The raw token is returned to the action; it is not stored in that row.

`loginAction` resolves the newly created token back to a `SessionPrincipal`, then `setSessionCookie` in [session.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/lib/session.ts) hands the raw token to the browser as `taskflow_session`. The cookie is HTTP-only, `SameSite=Lax`, scoped to `/`, secure in production, and expires with the session. The action result contains the principal—user ID, email, active organization ID and expiry—not the raw token. Although the form accepts “Keep me signed in,” the login and session-creation code does not use `rememberMe` to alter the 30-day lifetime.

After success, `LoginForm` navigates to its `next` prop. [login/page.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx) derives that destination from a same-site `next` path, defaulting to `/orgs`; it also redirects an already signed-in visitor there. At [orgs/page.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/app/(dashboard)/orgs/page.tsx), the app lists the user’s organizations, redirects directly to the workspace if there is exactly one, and otherwise presents a choice.

For a later request, [proxy.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/proxy.ts) first checks whether a non-public request has a nonempty session cookie; if not, it redirects to login with the requested path in `next`. Cookie presence alone is not proof of a live session. The authenticated [dashboard layout](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx) calls `getSessionPrincipal`, which reads the cookie, calls `resolveSession` to hash its token, and calls `findSessionByTokenHash`. That repository joins the matching session to its user and rejects missing or expired rows. `getSessionPrincipal` also checks expiry before returning the principal; a null result makes the dashboard layout redirect to `/login`. The [session API route](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/app/api/auth/session/route.ts) uses the same helper and returns either the principal or an unauthorized response.

The principal establishes identity globally; it has no role. For a workspace URL, the [organization layout](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/app/(dashboard)/%5BorgSlug%5D/layout.tsx) resolves the organization and calls `resolveActorForOrg(principal, orgSlug)` in `session-service.ts`. That function looks up the organization by slug and the user’s unarchived membership by organization and user ID. It requires the membership to be active, builds an `Actor` containing `userId`, `orgId` and the **current membership role**, checks the organization scope with `assertOrgScope`, and updates last-seen time. A missing organization or membership produces a 404 in the layout. Because the role comes from membership on resolution, it is not embedded in the session token.

The organization layout builds a feature-flag snapshot from the actor and organization, then passes the organization, actor and flags through `OrgProvider` and `DashboardShell` to [AppSidebar](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/components/domain/nav/app-sidebar.tsx). The sidebar calls `visibleNav` in [nav.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/config/nav.ts), which filters declared navigation items using their feature flags and `can()` permissions. For example, billing requires `org:manage_billing`, whose minimum role is owner, while feature-flag management requires admin.

The same `Actor` supports server authorization, not just sidebar presentation. [actor.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/lib/actor.ts) exposes `getActor` for slug-based requests, and [with-action.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts) resolves an actor before invoking an action handler. In [permissions.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/lib/permissions.ts), `can` delegates to `explain`: it rejects cross-organization resources first, then considers staff access, the action’s minimum role and applicable ownership exceptions. Services can use `assertCan` to enforce that decision.

One implementation detail affects ID-based actions: a newly created session has `activeOrgId: null`, and the current [switch-org action](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/4d60de3e-9a18-48d2-90ca-e929acfdc0f1/src/actions/organizations/switch-org.ts) checks the switch but does not persist an active organization. Slug-based workspace resolution still obtains its actor from the URL and membership; paths using `requireActorFor` require a non-null active organization.
